rows.why: When unapproved AI use is found, the business need or use that drove staff to it is recorded and re-evaluated against the organisation's purpose for AI.
AI tools, browser extensions, local models, agent frameworks and MCP clients or servers that staff use or install without approval are discovered and recorded in the inventory with their source.

Controls that keep staff to vetted AI services and components are identified and applied, such as allowlists of approved AI software and sources, extension control and blocking of unapproved AI services.
The likelihood and size of harm from unapproved AI use, such as data leaving through it or access it holds, are estimated from the usage found and from public incidents.

Staff are engaged regularly, for example through surveys, an amnesty or a request channel, to learn which AI tools they use and the needs behind them, and that feedback is recorded, surfacing shadow use that technical discovery misses.
Use of unapproved AI services and newly installed AI software is monitored continuously, for example through DNS, traffic, endpoint and DLP signals, so new shadow use is detected.
The controls that block unapproved AI services, extensions and self-installed AI software are tested to confirm they work and cannot simply be bypassed.
Logs attribute use of AI services and execution of self-installed AI software to a person, and are reviewed, so unapproved use can be traced and accounted for.
Personal and sensitive data sent to unapproved AI tools is detected and examined, so the privacy exposure from shadow use is known.
For each unapproved AI tool or experiment found, a decision is made and recorded whether it is brought into approval or must stop.
Unapproved AI tools, extensions, local models and MCP servers can be blocked, removed or quarantined, with someone responsible for doing it.
Access and tokens that staff granted to outside AI tools are reviewed, and revoked when the person leaves or changes role or the tool is not approved.
Incidents from unapproved AI use, such as sensitive data entered into a public tool or a malicious plugin or MCP server, are reported, tracked, contained and reviewed.
